topics.title: Math Question - Halloween candies
topics.text:
Mr. Cook bought a big box of his favorite Halloween candies to hand out to trick-or-trickers. However, he ate half of all the candies himself before the first child came and took her share. He ate half of what was left before the second child came, and half of what was left again before the third child came and took all of the remaining candies. If it is known that each child received the same number of candies, which of the following statements is certainly true about how many candies Mr. Cook originally bought?

A)	It is a multiple of $3$

B)	It is a multiple of $4$

C)	It is a multiple of $6$

D)	It is a multiple of $7$

E)	It is a multiple of $11$



Does anyone know how to solve this question? Thank you so much!

topics.title: A Innumerate's Journey
topics.text:
I feel obliged to write down my trip from being mediocre to slightly less mediocre, as I reach $1000$ posts, which is a pretty arbitrary number outside of base $10$.



Note that this retelling of a life may contain factual inaccuracies or alternative facts as my human brain slowly degrades memories.



 3rd Grade 

This is where the journey of a thousand problems first begin. I just learned how to multiply $2$ digit numbers together and I thought that I was pretty good at math. As such, I didn't really study much math outside of a weekly math class in a daycare on 5th grade level math.



In my elementary school, there was special math program which your admittance was based on a pretty long (1 and a half hour or so) standardized test done on a computer. The test would get harder if you did a bunch of problems correctly, and easier if you got a bunch of problems wrong, and you would be graded at the end with a final index. Since I was pretty impatient at that time, I managed to do it in half a hour, and subsequently got a bunch of problems wrong. Needless to say, I didn't make it into the math program, but two other kids from my grade did. They were pretty smart.



I was mildly upset, but didn't actually step up my mathematical game till much later.



 4th Grade 



Not much changed from 3rd Grade other than I learned a few more things about math like basic algebra. Also, I just finished reading my favorite underrated book series, Magyk.



Again, I did the math test thing to try to get into the math program. This time however, I made it probably because I spent more than 2 hours on it, thanks to some advice from my teacher.

In fact, I did so well, I jumped up $20$ or $30$ points on the test index.



I was introduced to a variety of mathematical subjects, such as triangular numbers and prime factorizations. We were handed out old AMC 8s and told to do them for homework. They were pretty fun for 4th Grade me since I got to brag that I was doing 8th grade math, but otherwise they were kind of boring.



I wasn't exactly the best in my class.

This was further exemplified as I got 10 on the AMC 8 that year, which was pretty average. The person who was first place in my class got a 16, I believe. I really didn't care about competition math, so I shrugged it off.

I would also like to point out that both my 4th and 5th grade AMC 10 were cancelled since someone messed up shipping the information. My math class was practically on the point of rioting. $:($



I also did MOEMS, and I got about 15 since I missed the first meet. I received a patch for my honorable effort.



Like before, I thought I was pretty good because of that giant jump, I got into the elite math program, and I was taking Pre-Algebra. This stagnated any actual attempts during my elementary years to do outside studying on math.





 5th Grade 



This was essentially the same as 4th Grade but I was getting better at math. I learned quadratics, formula for area of a circle and whatnot.



In school, we were taught basically the same things as last year, so I got better at those concepts and actually learned some. Also school-related, I did pretty well on the standardized test before mentioned during this year. The test has both a elementary and middle school version, and this year, we were taking the middle school instead of elementary since we were in a advanced math class. While most of my classmates' indexs fell, mine actually increased.



Outside of school, in the other math class, I learned Algebra 1.



I got a $11$ on the AMC 8, which shows the improvement in competition math between these two years. I then later got a $23$ on MOEMS, earning myself a silver pin along with 2 other fellows in my school.



Basically it.



Summer Between 5th And 6th Grade 



This is around the time I started getting serious about math. I started doing old AMC 8s, and a few AMC 10s. It was pretty much a ramble though, since I didn't time myself and just focused on doing problems. I think I even cheated a few times, changing a silly mistake to the right answer. I was also doing some Khan Academy stuff about trigonometry, which was not really helpful since I didn't learn Law of Sines or Law of Cosines or any basic identities.



The much more important thing that happened was that this was the first time I was exposed to AoPS. I needed a place to get those old AMCs and AoPS supplied it.



 6th Grade: The Early Months (August-November) 

My parents were pressuring me to get into the mathcount team, so I started actually preparing.



I mainly focused on doing these sets of 80 problems in 40 minutes things, which was supposed to help you with speed and accuracy in mathcount. This is also around the time I joined AoPS officially, with the self-deprecating username innumerateguy.  I also read some books about how to do specific types of mathcount problems which really didn't help.



For the next part of this section, you need some background knowledge. My school is a relatively competitive school to get onto the mathcount team. By that, I mean that you have to actually put in some effort. There is 5 practice tests, many 20-minute meetings, several 25 problems packets, three math competitions (one of them hosted by the school) which finally determine whether you get on the Mathcount team.



I did incredibly poor on almost all the practice tests which were around nationals level to my unexperienced eyes, but probably state level.

I however, did finish nearly all of the packets given and attended all the meetings. We were given mathcount minis, watched a video of Richard Rusczyk and turned in completed packets at the meetings, and the packets were usually centered around a certain topic, most likely the same topic as the mathcount mini in the previous meeting.





6th Grade: The AMC Revolution (November-January) 





To not bore you with specifics, here is a general overview of what I did:



We had a mock Mathcount competition in our school. I got 19th.



I did the AMC 8, and got 21.



We had some typical local competition. I got 1st, due to everyone else sillying.



We had some more mathcount practice tests, I failed.



I organized my archives and records on what practice tests I did by doing a total revamp of all my notebooks and got binders to categorize my tests.



I did nearly all of the AMC 10s, and some more mathcount tests



My mathcount prospects were looking pretty bad at this point, I have failed nearly all the practice tests and my only saving grace was the local math competition which could not possibly revive me from the dead.



And if you are interested, here is some more information about the mock mathcount competition:

We did sprint, countdown, team, and countdown all of which were made by a pro high schooler. It was a multi-school competition.

I was invited to a team by a person who got a perfect on the AMC 8, so that was encouraging. The team got too large though, so it eventually was split into two, one completely boys and the other partly girls.

I did really good at sprint, but not so well at target, and to be frank, my team pretty much failed. Countdown was exciting because a 6th grader was absolutely destroying these 7th and 8th graders.

It was fun.



 6th Grade: The Final Stand (January-Modern Era)





Turns out that I made a giant comeback in mathcount rankings. I managed to scrape myself into top 20 for mathcount, and was invited to do a practice sprint and countdown test (I would like to mention that the test-maker put in all the top 20 canidates' names into the problems. I was tied for 4th place (for the test) and I gotten into the top 10, and the mathcount team.



However, things would take a turn. Long story short, there was a miscalculation and I was cut from the team and became a alternate.



I saw a chance to redeem myself by doing well on the AMC 10s, and that did not go well. I made 4 sillies on the AMC 10A, and I missed a problem because that I didn't bubble in correctly. Then, I made 2 sillies on the AMC 10B, but wasted so much time on certain problems, I didn't really have a chance.



Nothing has really happened since, other than more preparation and waiting for the chance to gain redemption once again.

CMB Contest Problems1. The Evil Grinch has come and turned the wheels of all of the toy trains that the elves have built into trapezoids! The elves know that the area of the trapezoids are $136$, one of the bases is $15$ and the height is $8$. What is the length of the trapezoid's other base?



2. If the two statements below are true, which of the 3 following statements must also be true

(1) Lucas sometimes eats gingerbread cookies

(2) Erica never eats sugar cookies



I. Lucas never eats sugar cookies

II. Erica sometimes eats gingerbread cookies

III. Lucas and Erica never eat sugar cookies together



3. Calvin has $j$ amount of ornaments. If there are $j\cdot\frac 12$ ornaments in the first box and $7$ ornaments in the second box, how many ornaments are in the third box? $j$ is strictly less than $20$ and strictly more than $17$.



4. Mrs. Claus has baked many cookies and has placed then in boxes in a 5 shelf pantry. Unfortunately, there aren't any labels and Santa can't find the cookies he wants to give the elves. He knows that the macaroons are on the shelf directly below the oatmeal raisin cookies, the chocolate chip cookies are above the gingerbread cookies, and the oatmeal raisin cookies are 3 shelves below the sugar cookies. Which cookie type is on the third shelf?



5. Rob has 3 hats, 5 sweaters, 5 pants, and 2 pairs of shoes. How many ways can he dress himself on Christmas?



6. Santa is creating a plan on how to give all his gifts to the good kids. There are 196 countries in the world, and he can finish passing out gifts in one country in 5 minutes. Assuming it take him 1 minute to travel from 1 country to another, when will he finish passing out his gifts if he starts at 12:00 A.M.?



7. Solve for $x$. $7(2x-3)-4(x+5)=8(x+1)+3$



8. Santa has invited the elves to a party and they have to bring either candy canes or cookies or both. At the party, $\frac{3}{4}$ of the elves have brought candy canes with them, and $\frac{2}{5}$ of the elves brought cookies. What is the minimum number of elves at the party that brought both candy canes and cookies?



9. Find the sum: $\frac{1}{1\cdot3}+\frac{1}{3\cdot5}+....+\frac{1}{1997\cdot1999}$



10. Santa wants to know how many ways can he can arrange his reindeer, Dasher, Dancer, Prancer, Vixen, Comet, Cupid, Donner, and Blitzen. Can you help him figure out the answer?



11. Alex the elf has placed a certain amount of candy canes in a jar. The other elves must guess how many candy canes are inside with their 6 guesses. Alex tells them that the number is prime. The elves guess $13, 23, 37, 43$ and $53$. Alex tells them that 60% of their guesses are too low and all of them are incorrect. What must the elves' 6th guess be for it to be right?



12. Mrs. Claus is extremely happy with the elves' performance this year and has baked 100,000 cookies for them of 5 different types. $\frac{1}{5}$ of the cookies are chocolate chip, $\frac{8}{40}$ are sugar, $\frac{15}{50}$ are gingerbread, and $\frac{3}{30}$ are macaroons. How many cookies are peanut butter?



13. Santa has $100$ elves. He needs to distribute jobs to them. Scrubbing and washing Santa's sleigh takes $x$ amount of elves. Cleaning up the reindeers' waste takes twice the amount of elves as scrubbing and washing Santa's sleigh. Wrapping presents takes twice as many amount of elves as Cleaning up the reindeers' waste minus $7$ elves. Putting tags on presents and putting them in Santa's bag takes $5$ elves less then the amount of elves needed to scrub and wash Santa's sleigh. How many elves were needed for wrapping presents?



14. Santa hosts a Santa Quiz every year for the toy-making and gift-wrapping elves. Two thirds of the toy-making elves and 75% of the gift-wrapping elves passed the quiz and equal amount of toy-making and gift-wrapping elves passed. What is the least possible amount of elves who participated in the quiz?



15. Christmas is over and Santa wants to take a break by traveling. He plans on going to the Bahamas, Brazil, NYC, LA, Rome, Melbourne, and Japan. It takes him one day to go from one place to the next, and he stays at each location for two and a 3/7 week. (Santa can teleport to and from the North Pole in 0 seconds) If he departs the North Pole on January 3rd, 2017 at 7 AM, when will he get back to the North Pole? (your answer should be a date like 12/25)



16. There are 3 train companies in the North Pole: Reindeer Rail, Elf National, and Glacier Transportation. 3 trains are leaving the Santa Village Station tomorrow and all of them are heading to Elf Cross Station. The Reindeer Rail train leaves at 7AM at 40 mph. The Elf National train leaves at 8:30AM at 80 mph. The Glacier Transportation train leaves at 10AM at 120 mph. At what time will the each train catch up to each other? You should have a total of 3 answers: EN-RR, RR-GT, and EN-GT.



17. Papa Elf is trying to find which bank is best for saving his Elvens (currency used by Papa Elf). He has two options: the Elven Bank offers a 25% simple interest per year and the Golden Reindeer Bank offers a compound interest of 15% per year. If Papa Elf has 12,000 Elvens, how many years does it take for the interest from the 12,000 Elvens he put in the Golden Reindeer Bank to be greater than if he put the Elvens in the Elven Bank?



18. Santa has sent Ava, his elf assistant, to Candle Hill to discuss new holiday ideas with the Easter Bunny. He is currently looking for 3 temporary assistants and only 8 elves qualify for the position. How many different ways can Santa pick 3 elves to be his temporary assistants?



19. Ava the elf has 7 lamps labeled A through G arranged in a row. Each lamp has its own switch. Now lamps A, C, E, G are on and the other lamps are off. Ava starts to flip each switch from A to G the following way: if the lamp is on, she turns it off; if the lamp is off, she turns it on. She repeats the pattern until she flips the switches 2011 times. Which lamps are on finally?



20. The intersecting points of the equations $y=-5x+47$, $y=\frac{3}{2}x-18$ and $y=\frac{-7}{17}x+\frac{409}{17}$ forms the triangle $ABC$. What's the equation of the circle that pass through all three vertices of triangle $ABC$?



21. Santa has a cone with a radius of 6 inches and a height of 12 inches. He cuts it into three 4-inch high pieces with two cuts parallel to the base of the original cone. What's the ratio of the volume of the three pieces from the smallest to the largest?



22. In how many ways can three little pigs, a mother pig, and a father pig be arranged in seven different houses if multiple pigs can be in each house and the little pigs are identical?



23. Peter the elf pours 4 ounces of water into a bottle that can hold 8 oz. He then pours 4 oz of honey into a second bottle that also can hold 8 oz. He pours half of the contents of the first bottle into the second bottle and mixes the contents of the second bottle. Then he pours $\frac{1}{2}$ of the contents of second bottle back into the first bottle. What fraction of the contents of the first bottle is honey?



24. Sarah the elf is a very good abstract painter at Reindeer Studios in downtown North Pole. For her newest masterpiece, she is thinking about mixing any number of different colors from her elf palette together. Sarah can make a mixture as long as at least two of the colors are combined. If the number of possible mixtures is less than 500, what is the greatest number of colors Sarah could have in her elf palette?



25. Chester needs to choose 8 different types of candy from a box. The box only has peppermints, chocolates, gummy bears, and licorice. There at least 8 of each of the 4 candies. How many different assortments of 8 candies can be chosen?



Bonus!:

Calculators on not permitted on this problem:

(a) In triangle $ABC$, the lengths of sides $AB$ and $BC$ are $7$ and $5$, respectively. If $\angle{ABC}=75^{\circ}$, then what is the length of side $AC$? Express your answer in simplest radical form.

(b) Try to find a solution without the Law of Cosines!

topics.title: Prime number generator?
topics.text:
It started like this. I was bored in 1st period today, and saw the number 89 written on the board. Hmmmmm.... $17^2=289$... $289-200=89$ $200=\frac{20^2}{2}$. $17^2-\frac{20^2}{2}=89$ which is a prime. I wonder if $a^2-\frac{b^2}{2}$ makes primes.



After experimenting for a while, I see that $a$ must be odd, $b$ must be even, and $a$ and $b$ must be co prime. Can anyone prove or disprove that $a^2-\frac{b^2}{2}$ is a prime generator given the conditions imposed upon them?

topics.title: My most recent contest
topics.text:
Hello all,



My most recent contest, the 420 mock test, was canceled because of its inappropriateness of the title. Due to this, I will be kind of leaving AoPS for at least a while to learn more about math, though I may come on once in a while.



Here are the problems that I had made for the contest (none of them are inappropriate). They are ordered by problem difficulty, and are only composed of problems that I had made beforehand.

Problems1. What is the sum of the infinite geometric sequence $3+\frac{6}{7}+\frac{12}{49}+\dots$? Express your answer as a decimal to 2 decimal places (e.g 1 will not be accepted for 1.00).



2. What is the product of the last two non-zero digits of $420^{420^{420^{\dots}}}$, where there are $420$ $420$s in the expression?



3. How many positive integers less than $100$ have a prime number of divisors?



4. Three people A,B,C are building a wall at a speed of $1$,$2$, and $4$ fences per day respectively. If B can only work on every other day and C can only work on weekends, how many days will they need to build $420$ fences if they start on a Sunday?



5. Sam picks three real numbers in the range $[0,420]$. If the probability that the product of any two of the numbers is greater than the third is $\frac{m}{n}$, where $m$ and $n$ are positive integers, what is the remainder when $m+n$ is divided by $420$?



6. A regular pentagon with side length $2$ is constructed, and semicircles are drawn with diameters on all the sides such that no portion of the semicircles goes outside the pentagon. What is the area of all the intersections between the semicircles? If the answer can be expressed as $\frac{p\pi - \sqrt{q+\sqrt{r}}}{s}$, where $p,q,r,s$ are positive integers, what is the remainder when the minimum value of $p+q+r+s$ is divided by $420$?



7. Let $f(x)$ be a function such that for all integer $x,y$, this equation holds: $f(x)^{f(y)} = c$, where $c$ is a constant term. If $f(x)$ is nonconstant along the interval $[0,2017]$ inclusive, what is the remainder when the maximum value of $\sum_{k=0}^{2017} f(k)$ is divided by $420$?



BONUS:

Find, with proof, all functions $f(x)$ with integer $x$ such that $f(x)f(y)+1 = f(x+y)+f(xy)$.




Good luck solving the problems and good bye! :D

Do not pm anyone the solutions, just post them here, make sure to Click to reveal hidden texthide the solutions.

topics.title: Troll Questions
topics.text:
While I was bored doing AoPS homework, I came up with some troll questions. Enjoy!



Let $n$ be an integer such that $|n| \leqslant 1000$

Let $m$ be another integer satisfying the same property.

Find the product of all $m+n$.



There are 1000 people in a food fight, namely, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, ... , 1000. If person A hits person B, then person B must also hit person A in revenge. Given that any person $n$ hit $n$ people, what person got hit by the most people?



Every second, a lemming jumps off a cliff. Lemmings are incredibly fall resistant so the moment they hit the ground, they climb the trail back up the mountain to jump off the cliff again. One day, while the lemmings are doing their daily mountain jumping routine, a lemming decides to do something controversial: turn around and run the other way. Note that all lemmings run at the same speed and prior to the turning around, evenly spaced. If a lemming hits something, it will turn around and run in the other direction. What will happen when after the lemming decided to turn around?



There are 360 points evenly spaced around a circle, and numbered in clockwise order, 1 through 360. There is a pointer pointing at 1. Each turn, if it is pointing to an odd number, it can turn 1 degree, or it can choose to turn 99 degrees clockwise, but the next move must be counterclockwise. If the pointer is pointing at an even number, it must turn 9 degrees counterclockwise or one degree clockwise. What is the least number of moves it takes to reach 360?



At Troll Academy each person is given a locker number from 1 to 500. Inside each locker is a backpack numbered from 1 to 500, but not necessarily the same number as the locker. One day, Troll comes to Troll Academy, and finds that his backpack has been stolen and placed in another locker. Troll can see through slits in the locker, but the numbers on the backpacks are all too dark to read from the outside. In addition, all backpacks are the same color, size and shape. Troll does not know the locker combinations for the other lockers, and does not have time to ask 499 other people to open their lockers. Troll is friends with everyone at the school, so his search is not narrowed down. The air conditioning is too cold. How should Troll determine who stole his backpack?

topics.title: Winter Relay Race!
topics.text:
Rules and Summary of Winter Relay Race!Hello and welcome to a game of  Winter Relay Race. (12 days of Christmas!!!)



Here are the rules. There are 34 (or more) people and 17 pairs. Everyday after the game starts each pair of people will be given a Math Problem (Winter/Holiday Themed). If the pair correctly solves it then the next round they will get the next question (There will be 12 questions in total, one for each of the 12 days of Christmas!!!). We flip a fair coin 10 times. What is the probability that we get heads in at least 6 of the 10 flips?



In the solution, it says, "The probability that we flip at least 6 heads is equal to the probability that we flip at least 6 tails, by symmetry. The only other possibility is that we flip exactly 5 heads and 5 tails,...Therefore, 63/256 + 2p = 1".

topics.title: Im confused
topics.text:
Hi guys!



I know that $\cos(2x)=2\cos^2(x)-1$, and I am confused on what happens to $\cos(4x)$. Can someone tell me which of the below is correct?



First one:



$$\cos(4x)=2\cos^2(2x)-1$$$$\cos^2(2x)=\frac{\cos(4x)+1}{2}=2\cos^4(x)-1.$$

Second one:



$$\cos(4x)=2\cos^2(2x)-1$$$$\cos^2(2x)=\frac{\cos(4x)+1}{2}=(2\cos^2(x)-1)^2.$$

topics.title: Answer discrepancy on 2012 Nats Sprint?
topics.text:
Hello,



So I was checking my answer for 2012 Nats Sprint, and the answer key noted that there were two different accepted answers for #22, depending on the method you used to solve it. The official answer key said the answer is 12, but I got $\frac{20\sqrt{19}}{9}$. Unfortunately, Mathcounts didn't specify anything for the secondary answer on the answer key. Could someone confirm if my answer is correct, with my solution sketch? Thanks.



SketchWith POP, $MP=\frac{32}{3}$. Since $\triangle NKL$ is right, we can use Pythag to get $KL$, which is $2\sqrt{19}$. Since $\triangle PKL$ and $\triangle PNM$ are similar, and the ratio between sides is $\frac{10}{9}$, the answer is simply $2\sqrt{19}*\frac{10}{9}=\frac{20\sqrt{19}}{9}$.
